Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

achieve verb

also accomplish, attain, reach a goal, achievement, get somewhere, get anywhere, accomplish something

classical

Cic. Fam. 9.24.3: id forīs cēnitandō facillimē cōnsequēre
Traupman 179, 321: aliquid cōnsequī, to get somewhere, to accomplish something

cōnsequor, cōnsequī, cōnsecūtus sum

verb, third conjugation, deponent; with an accusative, or ut and the subjunctive · Conjugation on Wiktionary

achieve, attain, get

Lewis & Short: “to obtain, acquire, get, attain, reach”: of reaching what one wanted.

Other words

  • assequor (adsequor), assequī, assecūtus sum — attain, achieve (by effort)

    verb, third conjugation, deponent, transitive · also used · classical · Tac. Germ. 46.5–6: rem difficillimam adsecūtī sunt; Traupman 179, 353: magistrātum adsequī; Traupman 407 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: with the idea of active exertion, where cōnsequī is rather the attainment of a wish.

  • adipīscor, adipīscī, adeptus sum — reach, obtain

    verb, third conjugation, deponent, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 4: quam ut adipīscantur omnēs optant, eandem accūsant adeptam; Traupman 407 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Examples

  • cūrā ut valeās; id forīs cēnitandō facillimē cōnsequēre

    Look after your health; you’ll achieve that most easily by eating out a lot.Cic. Fam. 9.24.3

  • sēcūrī adversus hominēs, sēcūrī adversus deōs rem difficillimam adsecūtī sunt, ut illīs nē vōtō quidem opus esset

    Safe from men, safe from gods, they have achieved the hardest thing of all: they have no need even to pray for anything.Tac. Germ. 46.5–6

  • quam ut adipīscantur omnēs optant, eandem accūsant adeptam

    Everyone hopes to reach it, and complains of it once it is reached.Cic. Sen. 4

  • adsequī (adipīscī) magistrātum

    to win an officeTraupman 407
